item.title: Wealth Tax Debate, Midterm Investing, AI Anxiety
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Whitney Tilson, Stansberry Research Editor, and Stephanie Guild, Robinhood CIO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
item.description: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Notes on Being a Man', 'The Invisible Hand'
item.description: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss 'Notes on Being a Man' by Scott Galloway and 'The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth: How a Nineteenth-Century Novelist Taught the World Economics' by Jeanna Smialek. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Family Annual Healthcare Plan Now Costs More Than $28K
item.description: Bloomberg's John Tozzi joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The annual cost of a US family’s employer-provided healthcare plan reached an average $28,303 this year, 5% more than 2025, according to an annual survey conducted by health policy nonprofit KFF. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Data Centers Face Downgrade Risk Amid Local Pushback, S&P Says
item.description: Data centers face potential credit rating downgrades due to moratoriums and cancellations driven by public opposition, according to S&P Global Ratings.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb

item.title: Cidade do Pará rebelada contra política ambiental abraça Flávio
item.description: O repórter Fabiano Maisonnave conta sobre como a cidade do Pará rebelada contra política ambiental abraça Flávio. Com produção de Gisele Fernandes e edição de Mariana Lumy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robin Wigglesworth on the Importance of Curiosity
item.description: Barry speaks with Robin Wigglesworth, editor of Financial Times' Alphaville blog and author of the new book 'A Fabulous Debt: The Epic Story of How Bonds Built the Modern World'. They discuss the bond market as the engine of the global economy, why the 30-year mortgage is "a miracle of the modern world," and when we should actually start worrying about US debt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: National Wealth Tax Could Work: Tilson
item.description: Whitney Tilson, editor for Stansberry Research, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Tilson's hopes to bring Democrats back to the center, his personal investing strategy, and the potential for a national wealth tax. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: San Diego to Leave Muni Bond Group After SEC Oversight Concerns
item.description: The city of San Diego said it plans to withdraw from a group that helps issue and manage billions of dollars in municipal bonds after federal regulators raised concerns about the organization’s oversight.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford

item.title: Chipmakers Post Longest Weekly Drop Since November
item.description: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates. Brent crude settled near $117 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened supplies. Most S&P 500 firms fell even as selling pressure on tech shares abated. A gauge of chipmakers edged up, but posted its longest weekly drop since November. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.2%. Treasuries relinquished a portion of the previous session’s rally. Co-Host of Odd Lots, Joe Weisenthal says it's important to the US Economy that tech companies fire on all cylinders. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hedge Funds Are Record Short Natural Gas on Mild Winter Outlook
item.description: Hedge-fund managers have amassed a record short position in US natural gas on expectations for an unusually mild northern winter that points to anemic demand for the furnace and power-plant fuel.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: AI Trade Stumbles Again as Investors Rediscover Treasury Haven
item.description: According to the president of Blackstone Inc., there’s no bubble in artificial intelligence. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent isn’t seeing a “systemic problem” in the boom. But as hard as Wall Street brass works to tamp down concerns around the space, markets are refusing to be calmed.
item.dc:creator: Vildana Hajric and Lu Wang

item.title: SpaceX Shakes Up Telecom Stocks | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Jess Menton, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oncologists Cheer Melanoma Data
item.description: Leaked data from Moderna and Merck's highly anticipated melanoma vaccine trial has led to a rare disconnect between doctors, who celebrated the result, and Wall Street, which sold off the stocks. Normally results of such pivotal drug studies are binary, with doctors, patients and investors all learning whether a novel medicine will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives and forming the same conclusion. Instead, as reports leaked out on social media about the findings of the melanoma shot — days before the carefully scripted presentation planned for thousands of oncologists gathered in Madrid for the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting — realities diverged. Madison Muller, Bloomberg News Healthcare Reporter, reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Circuit - Season 6 Trailer
item.description: A Bloomberg Originals series hosted by Emily Chang that goes behind the scenes with founders, influencers and innovators. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NYSE Options Exchange Trading Halted by ‘Technical Issue’
item.description: A NYSE options exchange has suspended trading, causing other exchanges to disregard quotes from the venue.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Goyder

item.title: GM Shares Suffer Worst Week Since 2023 Amid Wider Autos Selloff
item.description: General Motors Co. shares recorded their worst week in nearly three years, leading a wider selloff in automotive stocks on Friday. Yet, bullish Wall Street analysts are doubling down on the carmaker.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fitzgerald and Paul Roman

item.title: Bolsonaro Trade Faces Reckoning in Too-Close-to-Call Brazil Vote
item.description: Wall Street strategists who recommended loading up on Brazil assets after Flávio Bolsonaro emerged as the frontrunner for president are about to see if they led clients astray or to profits ahead of Sunday’s too-close-to-call runoff.
item.dc:creator: Vinícius Andrade, Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo, Barbara Nascimento and Leda Alvim

item.description: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
item.description: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)
